page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Powered by KVM virtualization, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance offers no local SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average single-threaded performance alongside lower multi-core scalability. In single-core tests, the instance records a Geekbench score of 1305.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 23.96 GB/sec, placing both in the middle performance tier. PassMark CPU encryption achieves 4270.77, while PassMark memory score reaches 1865.07. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput drops relative to higher-density instances, with multi-core stress-ng scores at 1535.77 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 18.36 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth measures 31.36 GB/sec for uncached reads and 16.16 GB/sec for uncached writes. Static web serving throughput reaches 4.07 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivers 3.57 million operations per second. From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides a entry point for compute workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without local storage overhead. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached block storage for persistent data. This profile makes ecs.c6a.xlarge appropriate for light web serving, basic batch jobs, single-threaded processing utilities, and small microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors operating at 2.6 GHz under KVM virtualization. Built on x86_64 architecture, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Instruction support includes AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA, with an L3 cache capacity of 16 MB. The instance includes no local storage and maintains a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show moderate single-threaded capability, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 23.96 GB/sec. Multi-threaded workloads show lower performance density, reflected by a multi-core stress-ng score of 1535.77 and Redis throughput of 3.57 million SET operations per second. Offering dedicated CPU compute resources without local disk costs, ecs.c6a.xlarge is suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded automation tasks, CI/CD utility nodes, and small-scale backend microservices.
